newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas ends lower, stuck in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas ends lower, stuck in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures wavered only slightly to settle lower Tuesday, cornered by a steady cash market and technical selling, industry sources said.
November finished 2.9 cents weaker at $2.185 per million British thermal units. December settled down 2.4 cents at $2.36, while other deferreds showed only minor changes.
Sources also attributed the range-bound session to a significant drop in trading volume this afternoon following a frenzy of buying interest shortly after the opening.
Technically, traders said November was still stuck in the $2.14-2.24 range as it awaits clearer signs from the cash market.
Some traders suggested that a break through the $2.161 level would add more weight to the reversal to the downside theory following November's reluctance to break through today's early high of $2.26.
Further support was seen in the $2.04-2.06 area and then at $2. The major resistance level was still pegged at $2.305.
Cash prices on the Gulf Coast pipes held steady in the high-$1.80s to mid-$1.90s. Midcontinent prices were in the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s.
NYMEX said an estimated 25,971 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 23,726. The 12-month strip slipped 0.6 cent to $2.116.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas finished one cent higher at $1.005, boosted by colder-than-normal temperatures in the Canadian province. NYMEX said an estimated 71 lots exchanged hands.
Physical prices at the AECO-C Hub were also stronger in the C$1.30 per gigajoule area, up about five cents from Monday.
NYMEX November Permian natgas settled a half-cent firmer at $1.865 after hitting a high of $1.88 earlier in the day. NYMEX said an estimated 16 contracts traded.
Physical gas prices in the basin were talked about 10 cents higher in the low-to-mid $1.80s.

On the KCBT, November ended up 1.5 cents at $1.955, paring earlier gains to as high as $1.985. Deferreds were on either side of unchanged. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.4 cents to 23 cents (NYMEX premium).
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association report still ranged from 63 to 80 billion cubic feet, with the bulk of the estimates closer to the higher end of the range.
